subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: Should explicit `pty:true` in sandboxed exec warn and continue without PTY, fail closed, or wait for backend-supported sandbox PTY behavior?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but the fix defines user-visible behavior at a sandbox execution boundary where warning, rejection, and future backend support have different security and compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Warn and Continue
options.body: Preserve current sandbox execution while adding a visible warning, docs, and regression coverage for ignored sandbox PTY requests.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject explicit sandboxed PTY requests so callers cannot mistake pipe execution for a terminal session.

options.title: Design Sandbox PTY
options.body: Keep this as broader backend-specific work instead of only documenting the current suppression.

recommendation.title: Warn and Continue
recommendation.body: Preserve current sandbox execution while adding a visible warning, docs, and regression coverage for ignored sandbox PTY requests.

likelyOwner.reason: The original exec PTY support and later exec runtime extraction make this the strongest history-backed owner for the behavior contract decision.
